title: Investigating H2 Production Kinetics of Nano-Si Powders in Water via Liquid-Phase TEM
content: The silicon-water (Si-H2O) reaction is well known for its high hydrogen (H2) yield and cost-effectiveness, making it a promising candidate for on-demand H2 production. In this study, we utilize liquid-phase transmission electron microscopy (LPTEM) to investigate the reaction kinetics of Si-H2O at various pH levels. Our analysis reveals two distinct reaction pathways: at lower pH, crystalline Si primarily forms water-soluble SiO2(OH)2²⁻, while at higher pH, it yields solid SiO2.
